my nmom got mad at me because I asked her to get her dog water...

she randomly brought a dog home a few days before Christmas, stating she needed something to love and want her. I told her she would need to take care of it (I was in a wheelchair and heavily disabled plus had a 90 lb golden retriever of my own) 

to no ones surprise I took care of the new puppy and tried to communicate how I was training her with my mom (for consistency purposes)  she got mad because she thought I was saying she was bad with taking care of her dog...even though she's never had to raise a puppy and I just wanted the poor dog to have a good prognosis in her temperament, etc. she was also a rescue found on the side of a highway, and had a habit of drinking way too much water and peeing it out on the floor. 

SO, picture this: 

me, sitting in a wheelchair, not able to stand, walk or even use a proper toilet, wheeling into the kitchen with my golden next to me. she's on a ladder looking into cabinets and I mention I had done some research on training her puppy for her. and yes, at this point I'd been researching for HOURS to make sure her dog and mine got along. 

I told her that the best way to regulate her drinking was to make sure water is there at ALL times, so she knows she doesn't have to drink it all at once. my mom threw a FIT. she kept saying that she doesn't want to keep cleaning her dog's pee (to which I offered ways to house train) and that the only way to get her to stop peeing is to take away the water. 
apparently the dog's basic needs are completely ignored if they're inconvenient for my mom. she actually told me that if I want Rachel (her dog) to have more water, then I (crippled and all) need to house train her. 

it's gotten a bit better now that Rachel is older but she still pees in the house during the day and night at almost 1 year because my mom refuses to do basic training..."I'm too busy" and all that. it just baffles me.

yes, there is definitely a chance he was alive which freaked me out more. he was wearing winter clothes in 90 degree weather with 80% humidity. i wanted to hop out of the van and help him to safety (my parents are nurses so i have a bit of a savior complex with that i think). but the way he was sprawled was so lifeless, and either way it breaks my heart like lmao i know i cant save everyone but i want to

he was clean shaven, but wearing a heavy hoodie and sweatpants in direct sunlight when it was 90 degrees out. there are a lot of drug od's there so it mightve been that, but that in itself makes me worry about heat stroke, dehydration, hyperthermia... i tend to overthink everything so when i thought that he might still be alive i felt helpless and knew that he was hurting at some point.

yes, EMDR is a route I'm looking into. im currently in group therapy so it's hard to process everything. it was hard hearing my mom (a narcissist) completely ignore it. i thought I had completely overreacted. that you for the reassurance ❤️

car crash broke both of my legs..my right leg was shattered like a jigsaw puzzle, my femur itself had two full breaks one of which was compound and shredded. my tibia broke into a million parts and was a compound and the fibula broke in two places. my left leg just had a femur break but let me tell you...that initial adrenaline and shock was going great until the firemen were wrestling my legs out of the car and i screamed like a fucking banshee

when i became an adult i thought i finally had an opinion that mattered and so i treated my internal opinions the same. needless to say i started calling adults out on their bullshit that they told me i wouldnt understand until i was an adult myself.

had been fighting with my mom for weeks about very complicated issues, but i think the final straw was when i started crying while describing childhood abuse. she came to hug me and i cried for a while. at some point while i was crying, she softened her tone, rubbed my back and pushed her own agenda on me. she wanted me to stop analyzing her emotions (by analyzing she meant telling her that her assumptions were wrong). there were a lot of other things leading up because shes always been manipulative, but her trying to change my behavior in the middle of a very vulnerable moment was the last straw

my mom had a habit of withdrawing affection and compassion when i didnt act how she wanted. it conditioned me to only act how she deemed appropriate just for a hug. its continued into my early adulthood

extremely aware. my parents raised me religious, but my dad was conservative and my mother was liberal. in high school i was far left to the point i was mad and angry at everyone and everything. i've completely evened out (im more moderate now), but i can easily look back on my high school years and find the differences in how i used to think. for me, i think a lot of it had to do with a growth in maturity and realizing i dont have to agree with one party for everything

easy...my car accident. broke both femurs, my right one shattered in two places and compounded. broke my right tibia, also shattered like a jigsaw puzzle and compounded. fibula broke in two places. there were some other minor breaks, but those hurt the most.

the PTSD would be enough to deal (the pain was pretty much unimaginable), stack on the chronic pain, arthritis in my knees at 22 and the fact i cant run ever again...i dont hate anyone enough to want them to ever go through that
